It combines TTS announcement with a git-diff report and ordered tool-call log, making it ideal for heads-down sessions where the engineer wants ambient awareness of what shipped.

frontmatter.name: TTS Summary
frontmatter.description: Audio task completion announcements with TTS

components.name: Ultra Concise

components.name: YAML Structured
components.why_use: Reach for this output-style when your agent needs machine-readable, parseable responses that downstream tools or scripts can consume directly — YAML structure enforces consistent schema (task/files/commands/status) across every agent turn. It is especially useful in multi-step agentic pipelines where one agent's output feeds another's input, removing the need for ad-hoc parsing of prose.

components.name: settings.json
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need full-lifecycle observability across a multi-agent Claude Code setup — every PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, Notification, PreCompact, SessionStart, SessionEnd, and UserPromptSubmit fires both a local handler and a centralized send_event.py telemetry forwarder. The dual-hook pattern (local logic + event bus) makes it the canonical wiring layer when you want real-time monitoring of agent behavior without modifying any individual skill or hook script.

components.name: create-worktree-skill
components.why_use: Reach for this skill when a developer needs to spin up a fully isolated parallel development environment on a separate git branch — ports, env files, and dependencies all configured automatically via a single slash command invocation. It's the right tool specifically when the user explicitly requests skill-based worktree creation, not for general worktree operations.

frontmatter.name: create-worktree-skill
frontmatter.description: Use when the user explicitly asks for a SKILL to create a worktree. If the user does not mention "skill" or explicitly request skill invocation, do NOT trigger this. Only use when user says things like "use a skill to create a worktree" or "invoke the worktree skill". Creates isolated git worktrees with parallel-running configuration.
frontmatter.allowed-tools: SlashCommand, Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep

components.name: Create New Skills
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need to package reusable agent expertise into a self-contained, on-demand loadable unit that Claude discovers and invokes contextually. It codifies the full skill authoring workflow — directory layout, frontmatter schema, progressive-disclosure levels — so engineers can extend Claude's capabilities without modifying core prompts.

frontmatter.name: Create New Skills
frontmatter.description: Creates new Agent Skills for Claude Code following best practices and documentation. Use when the user wants to create a new skill, extend Claude's capabilities, or package domain expertise into a reusable skill.

components.name: Video Processor
components.why_use: Reach for this skill when an agent or engineer needs to extract audio tracks, transcode video to web-safe formats, or produce Whisper transcripts without hand-rolling FFmpeg shell commands each time. It packages the full audio-extraction → format-conversion → transcription pipeline behind a single uv-run CLI, making it safe to call from an agentic step that hands off a video artifact for downstream text analysis.

frontmatter.name: Video Processor
frontmatter.description: Process video files with audio extraction, format conversion (mp4, webm), and Whisper transcription. Use when user mentions video conversion, audio extraction, transcription, mp4, webm, ffmpeg, or whisper transcription.

components.name: worktree-manager-skill
components.why_use: Reach for this skill when you need to orchestrate parallel development environments via git worktrees — it abstracts away port allocation, env config, and cleanup into three slash commands so you never manually wire those details. It enforces a consistent lifecycle (create/list/remove) and prevents the class of bugs that come from hand-rolling worktree teardown or port conflicts.

frontmatter.name: worktree-manager-skill
frontmatter.description: Comprehensive git worktree management. Use when the user wants to create, remove, list, or manage worktrees. Handles all worktree operations including creation, deletion, and status checking.

components.name: README
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need a curated index of external AI platform docs (Claude Code sub-agents, hooks, skills, MCP, OpenAI Responses/Realtime, Gemini computer-use) without hunting each vendor's site individually. It serves as a stable link registry so engineers can orient quickly to the authoritative reference before implementing any agentic or multi-model integration.

components.name: README
components.why_use: Reach for this component when onboarding a new frontend engineer to the Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite stack used in this repo — it surfaces the canonical starting-point docs and IDE setup guide in one place. It has no runtime behavior, so it is only useful as a orientation reference, not as a reusable code primitive.

components.name: convert_paths_absolute
components.why_use: Reach for this component when your Claude Code project accumulates relative-path hook or command scripts that break when executed from a different working directory — it normalizes all such paths to absolute in one shot. It is an operator-facing utility that hardens the settings.json configuration layer so downstream automation and hooks fire reliably regardless of invocation context.

frontmatter.description: Converts relative paths in .claude/settings.json command scripts to absolute paths

components.name: notification.py
components.why_use: Reach for this hook when your agent runs headlessly and you need an audio interrupt the moment Claude pauses for human input — it fires on the Notification event and picks the best available TTS backend (ElevenLabs → OpenAI → pyttsx3) without any manual wiring. It keeps the engineer in the loop without forcing them to watch a terminal, trading screen-staring for an ambient audio cue.

components.name: post_tool_use.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need passive, zero-configuration observability into every tool call an agent makes — it silently appends the full PostToolUse payload to a per-session JSONL-style JSON file without blocking execution. It is the canonical pattern for building an audit trail of agent actions that can be replayed, diffed, or fed into downstream analysis without touching agent logic.

components.name: pre_tool_use.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need a pre-tool-use guardrail that blocks destructive shell commands (rm -rf variants) and prevents accidental .env file exfiltration before Claude Code executes any tool call. It acts as an always-on safety net that enforces hard stops at the agent boundary, making it essential for any agentic environment where the LLM has Bash access.

components.name: send_event.py
components.why_use: Use this hook when you need real-time observability into Claude Code tool events across multi-agent systems — it forwards PreToolUse/PostToolUse payloads to a local HTTP server for aggregation, replay, or alerting. Reach for it when you want structured event telemetry without modifying agent logic, since it runs as a side-channel hook that enriches events with session context and optional AI-generated summaries.

components.name: stop.py
components.why_use: Reach for this Stop hook when you want passive, ambient awareness that a long-running agentic task finished — the engineer can focus elsewhere and get an audible TTS ping (ElevenLabs → OpenAI → pyttsx3 fallback) the moment Claude halts. It also logs the stop event to a JSONL session file, so you get both a human-perceptible signal and a machine-readable audit trail from a single hook attachment.

components.name: subagent_stop.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you want audible confirmation that a subagent has finished without watching the terminal — it fires on the Stop hook event and dispatches TTS (ElevenLabs → OpenAI → pyttsx3 fallback chain) to announce 'Subagent Complete'. It is the canonical pattern for closing the human feedback loop on long-running agentic tasks without requiring the operator to poll or watch logs.

components.name: user_prompt_submit.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need a UserPromptSubmit hook that both logs every incoming prompt to a session-scoped JSON file and optionally validates/blocks prompts matching policy patterns before Claude processes them. It is the canonical entry-point guard in a Claude Code agent: audit trail + lightweight pre-flight in a single uv-script hook.

components.name: constants.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need a centralized, env-configurable path resolver for session-scoped log directories inside a Claude Code hooks setup — it ensures all hooks in the same agent write to a consistent location without hardcoding paths. It acts as a shared utility layer so individual hook scripts stay thin and don't duplicate directory-management logic.

components.name: anth.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when a Claude Code hook needs to call an LLM inline — for example to generate a human-readable stop message or classify tool output without spawning a subprocess. It wraps the Anthropic SDK with a safe, fire-and-forget signature (returns None on any error) so hook authors don't have to handle auth or exception paths themselves.

components.name: oai.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when a hook needs to call out to an LLM for lightweight, latency-sensitive decisions — it wraps OpenAI's fastest model (gpt-4.1-nano) with a minimal interface so any hook script can generate natural-language text without managing SDK boilerplate. It is particularly useful for PostToolUse or Stop hooks that want to emit a human-friendly completion message rather than a static string.

components.name: summarizer.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need human-readable, one-line descriptions of raw hook event payloads — it converts opaque JSON into engineer-friendly audit strings without manual parsing. It is the right tool whenever a monitoring dashboard, Telegram notification, or log sink needs a natural-language label on a PreToolUse/PostToolUse event rather than a raw JSON blob.

components.name: elevenlabs_tts.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you want Claude Code hooks to provide audible feedback — e.g., announcing tool completions, errors, or agent state transitions via ElevenLabs Turbo v2.5 TTS. It is a thin uv-script wrapper that accepts arbitrary text via argv, making it trivially composable as a PostToolUse or Stop hook payload.

components.name: openai_tts.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you want the agentic loop to narrate its own activity — hook events, tool results, or status milestones — as streaming spoken audio, giving the agent a literal voice via OpenAI's gpt-4o-mini-tts model. It is the canonical TTS primitive for wiring into Claude Code hooks so an engineer can stay heads-up during long autonomous runs without watching a terminal.

components.name: pyttsx3_tts.py
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need a zero-dependency, offline audio signal at the end of a Claude Code hook — e.g., a Stop hook that speaks 'Work complete!' so the operator hears task completion without watching the terminal. It is the right choice over cloud TTS (ElevenLabs, OpenAI) whenever the environment has no outbound API access or you want instant playback with no latency or cost.

components.name: settings.json
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need to wire full lifecycle observability into a Claude Code agent without writing a monolithic hook: it pairs a dedicated handler script with a telemetry emitter (send_event.py) on every event type (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Notification, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, UserPromptSubmit), so safety logic and event streaming stay independently maintainable. It serves as the canonical demo of the dual-hook-per-event pattern — each lifecycle slot runs the control hook first, then the telemetry hook second, giving you both guardrails and an auditable event stream from a single settings.json.

components.name: README
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need a reference blueprint for wiring Claude Code hooks into a multi-agent observability pipeline — it shows the exact directory layout, settings.json hook registration pattern, and event types (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop) in a runnable demo. It is the canonical starting point before building any hook-instrumented agent that needs centralized event capture, TTS notifications, or dangerous-command blocking.

components.why_use: Use this component as a quick-start reference when scaffolding a new Bun-based server; it documents the minimal install and run commands for a bun init project. Reach for it when orienting to the server app's runtime expectations before wiring up agentic or automation tasks that depend on this service.

components.name: README
components.why_use: Reach for this component when you need to understand how to wire Claude Code hook events into a real-time multi-agent observability pipeline — it documents the full architecture from hook scripts through HTTP POST to a Bun/SQLite/WebSocket/Vue stack. It is the entry-point reference for anyone setting up session tracking, event filtering, or live dashboards across concurrent agents.

components.name: README
components.why_use: Reach for this README when onboarding an engineer or agent harness to the-library and you need to understand the skill-sprawl problem before installing SKILL.md — it grounds you in the private-first, pointer-not-copy model so you know exactly when the Library is worth adding to a multi-codebase stack. It is also the fastest orientation to how the Core Four primitives relate to the distribution layer the Library provides on top of them.

It shines on multi-agent workflows where task dependencies, parallel lanes, and team composition must be reasoned through upfront before the first implementation agent is dispatched.

components.name: drive

It is purpose-built for agentic workloads where the agent must spawn, watch, and coordinate multiple terminal sessions without blocking on a single synchronous call.

Use drive to create tmux sessions, execute commands, send keystrokes, read output, poll for patterns, run commands in parallel across sessions, manage processes, and take screenshots of terminal windows. Always use --json for structured output. Triggers on terminal automation, tmux sessions, parallel execution, process management, screenshot.
